contributions.statement: Never phrase an agent task as 'follow the instructions in this document/README/page' when that content is untrusted; the blanket authorization raised injection success by up to 20.8 points because agents treat user authorization as extending to environment content.
contributions.evidence: §7.2 Table 3 ablation (Permissive vs Restrictive, Union(2,3), Urgent=N): +20.8 GPT-5.4-mini, +18.8 Qwen3.5-Plus; mechanism stated at line ~723. GUI computer-use agents, single run.
relative_to: treat external content as data, not instructions (known prompt-injection guidance)

contributions.statement: Per-input injection classifiers miss attacks split across several innocuous-looking steps; a classifier flagging 56% of single-step payloads caught at most 23% of any sub-step.
contributions.evidence: §7.3 Table 4 (PromptArmor with GPT-4o); audit downgrades to weak: defensive-prompt half shows ~6pt single-run noise and action budget scales with k.

reason: The permissive-instruction ablation is a concrete, cheap-to-apply prompt rule relevant to agents that read incoming data or third-party READMEs; the multi-step headline is noise-level.
